chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Himran, on the authority of his father that Abi Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon them) said:

There are no two believers who are on no talking terms for more than three days except that they are estranged from each other on the third day. He was asked, 'O son of the Messenger of God, this is the state of the oppressor, but what about the oppressed one?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'What is it with the oppressed one that he does not go to the oppressor and say: I am the oppressor, so that they reconcile?'

key_terms.اهْتَجَرَا: to be estranged or cut off communication

ai.seo_question: How should an oppressed believer initiate reconciliation with the oppressor according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to establish the three-day limit for *hiجر* (estrangement) between believers, emphasizing that the burden of reconciliation falls primarily on the oppressed party to prevent prolonged discord. The Imam’s instruction for the oppressed to say 'I am the oppressor' is a practical application of *adab* (etiquette) and humility, encouraging the initiation of peace even when one is technically in the right, thereby prioritizing communal harmony over strict justice. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on active conflict resolution and the spiritual merit of lowering one's ego for the sake of Allah.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-251 Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamedany - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Himran, on the authority of his father that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“I despise any two believers who are on no talking terms for more than three days.” He (MGB) was asked, “Well. This is fair enough for the oppressor. But what about the oppressed one?” The Imam (MGB) said, “Why doesn’t the oppressed one go to the oppressor and ask him to excuse him so that they are on talking terms as before?”
